preamble: Voicing and spirantization of the uvular stop [q] to the voiced uvular fricative [ʁ] is intervocalic lenition. It is best documented in Kipchak Turkic: in Kazakh, a stem-final /q/ is realized as [ʁ] (spelled ғ) when a vowel-initial suffix follows. Classical Arabic /q/ in Sudanese Arabic gives velar [ɣ] rather than uvular [ʁ], so it belongs in a different cell. Documented cases of exactly q > ʁ outside Turkic are scarce.

examples.note: Stem-final /q/ becomes [ʁ] (ғ) between vowels when a vowel-initial possessive suffix is added; the stop is kept before consonant-initial suffixes (dative аяққа ayaqqa, locative аяқта ayaqta).
